notes: relevant_chunk_ids: fill these in manually after running retrieval and inspecting which chunks actually came back for each question. These are required for precision@k and recall@k in run_eval.py.
expected_answer: a reference answer for groundedness checking — does not need to be verbatim, just captures the key claims the agent should make.
should_decline: true means the agent should return its hardcoded decline message, not attempt an answer.
category — easy: answer lives in one chunk; hard: requires synthesizing across chunks; out-of-scope: not in corpus; malformed: API-layer boundary test (rejected before reaching the agent).

questions.question: How do I add a background task to a path operation?
questions.expected_answer: Import BackgroundTasks from fastapi, add a parameter of type BackgroundTasks to your path operation function, then call background_tasks.add_task(fn, *args) to schedule a function to run after the response is sent.

questions.question: How do I set a custom response status code?
questions.expected_answer: Use the status_code parameter on the path operation decorator, e.g. @app.post('/items', status_code=201). You can use integer literals or the constants in fastapi.status.

questions.question: How do I validate a query parameter with a regex pattern?
questions.expected_answer: Use Query() with the pattern parameter, e.g. Query(pattern='^fixedquery$'). FastAPI will validate the value against the regex and return a 422 if it doesn't match.

questions.question: How do I add CORS middleware to a FastAPI app?
questions.expected_answer: Import CORSMiddleware from fastapi.middleware.cors and add it with app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=[...], allow_methods=[...], allow_headers=[...]). Setting allow_origins=['*'] permits all origins.

questions.question: How do I return a custom error response with HTTPException?
questions.expected_answer: Raise HTTPException with a status_code and a detail string, e.g. raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='Item not found'). FastAPI catches it and returns a JSON response with that status code and detail.

questions.question: How do I combine path parameters with numeric validation and a request body model in the same endpoint?
questions.expected_answer: Declare the path parameter with Path() and pass numeric constraints like ge, le, gt, lt. Declare the body as a Pydantic BaseModel parameter. FastAPI distinguishes them by type: path params match the URL template, body params are Pydantic models, query params are everything else.

questions.question: What's the difference between using response_model and just returning a dict, and how do I exclude unset fields from the response?
questions.expected_answer: response_model validates and filters the response — only fields declared in the model are included, extra fields from the return value are stripped. To exclude fields the client didn't set, use response_model_exclude_unset=True on the decorator, which omits any field whose value was not explicitly provided.

questions.question: How do I serve static files in FastAPI?
questions.expected_answer: Import StaticFiles from fastapi.staticfiles and mount it with app.mount('/static', StaticFiles(directory='static'), name='static'). FastAPI will serve all files in that directory under the /static path prefix.

questions.question: How do I read a custom request header in a path operation?
questions.expected_answer: Declare a parameter with type annotation and Header() as the default, e.g. user_agent: str | None = Header(default=None). FastAPI converts underscores to hyphens automatically, so user_agent maps to the User-Agent header.

questions.question: How do I accept a file upload in FastAPI?
questions.expected_answer: Declare a parameter with type UploadFile (or bytes) and File() as the default. UploadFile gives you the filename, content_type, and an async read() method. You must also install python-multipart for form/file parsing to work.

questions.question: How do I group path operations under a tag in the OpenAPI docs?
questions.expected_answer: Pass a tags parameter to the path operation decorator, e.g. @app.get('/items', tags=['items']). All operations with the same tag are grouped together in the auto-generated /docs UI.

questions.question: How do I add custom middleware that runs on every request in FastAPI?
questions.expected_answer: Decorate an async function with @app.middleware('http'). It receives the request and a call_next function — call await call_next(request) to get the response, then return it. You can read/mutate the request before and the response after.

questions.question: How do I accept both form fields and a file upload in the same endpoint?
questions.expected_answer: Declare parameters using Form() for text fields and File() or UploadFile for the file in the same function signature. You cannot mix a JSON body with form data in one request — all fields must come from the form. python-multipart is required.

questions.question: How do I write a test for a FastAPI endpoint, and what client should I use?
questions.expected_answer: Import TestClient from fastapi.testclient and pass your app instance to it. Use client.get(), client.post() etc. in your test functions — no running server needed. TestClient wraps httpx and runs requests synchronously, so standard pytest test functions (not async) work fine.

questions.question: What does jsonable_encoder do and when do I need it instead of just returning a Pydantic model directly?
questions.expected_answer: jsonable_encoder converts a Pydantic model (or any object) into a JSON-compatible dict — handling types like datetime, UUID, and Decimal that are not natively JSON-serializable. FastAPI calls it internally before sending a response, so you rarely need it explicitly unless you're storing the data somewhere (e.g. a database or an in-memory dict) before returning it.
